valuation_philosophy: This is NOT a discounted-FCF model. Me Today has never generated positive free cash flow or a profit from continuing operations in any period on record, accumulated losses are $54.5m, and the share count is not a continuous series (1-for-5 consolidation Apr-2020, 1-for-100 consolidation Jan-2024, then a near-doubling via rights issue Nov-2025) -- discounting today's negative FCF at a Gordon-growth terminal value, or computing per-share CAGRs across the consolidation breaks, produces arithmetically meaningless output. Instead this is a scenario-weighted PATH-TO-BREAKEVEN model: (1) project continuing-operations revenue and EBITDA margin to the point EBITDA turns positive under each scenario, referencing management's own FY2026 guidance (gross revenue >$7.4m, EBITDA loss <$1.6m, both raised twice and reaffirmed 29-Jul-2026); (2) build owner FCF from that EBITDA path (D&A, tax, capex, working-capital-on-growth); (3) walk the cash balance year by year to determine whether and when the company needs external capital, modelling the 95.522m warrants (Series 1 exercisable 1-30 Oct 2026, Series 2 exercisable Oct 2027, both struck at $0.06, currently OUT-OF-THE-MONEY against a $0.052 share price) conditionally -- they exercise (cash in, shares out) only in scenarios where the price has re-rated above the strike by the relevant window, and expire worthless (no cash, no dilution) otherwise, in which case a discounted dilutive placement bridges the shortfall instead; (4) value the resulting Year-5 EBITDA with an exit EV/EBITDA multiple (Gordon growth is unusable this close to breakeven -- a small change in terminal growth swings a near-zero perpetuity denominator wildly) discounted at a scenario-specific cost of equity built up from illiquidity, pre-profitability, concentration and governance premiums (20-26% range, well above a normal WACC); (5) divide by the YEAR-5 diluted share count, which differs materially by scenario because dilution is itself a modelled outcome, not a constant. The two near-term events that will resolve most of the uncertainty in this model are the audited FY2026 result (due to NZX before 31 August 2026 -- imminent) and whether the shares trade above $0.06 before the Series 1 warrant window closes on 30 October 2026.

sanity_check.applicable_multiples: P/E and EV/EBITDA are UNDEFINED for MEE.NZ -- net income and EBITDA are negative in every historical period in the CSV (FY2020-FY2025, H1-2026 continuing ops all loss-making before the one-off King Honey gain). No multiple-based sanity check on earnings or EBITDA is possible; P/Sales and P/Book are used instead.
sanity_check.current_p_s_note: Market cap $4.915m / net debt $0.024m => EV $4.939m against FY2026 guided net revenue ~$7.5m = EV/Sales ~0.66x. This is a modest multiple for a growth story -- consistent with the market already pricing meaningful dilution/execution risk rather than extrapolating the guidance-raise trend at face value.
sanity_check.current_p_b_note: Market cap $4.915m / book equity $3.055m (31-Dec-2025) = 1.61x P/B. Book value only turned positive in H1-2026 following the non-cash $4.14m King Honey deconsolidation gain; NTA is essentially the book value since intangibles are only $0.246m.
sanity_check.diagnosis: Base-case scenario IV ($0.0144) sits well below the current price ($0.052, -72%) primarily because of modelled dilution (94.5m -> 169.3m shares, +79%) needed to bridge FY2027-28 cash burn before EBITDA turns durably positive, not because the underlying operating trajectory is doubted -- FY2026 guidance has genuinely been raised twice and reaffirmed. The market's own EV/Sales of 0.66x suggests it is not pricing a smooth, low-dilution path to profitability either. This divergence is disclosed rather than smoothed away: it is the central finding of the model, not an error to fix.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- outputs are internally consistent (P/S and P/B anchors used in place of undefined P/E and EV/EBITDA; bear-case negative equity value floored at $0.00/share rather than reported as a negative per-share number, which would be meaningless for an equity claim).

wacc_rationale.method: Additive cost-of-equity build (not a debt/equity-weighted WACC in the conventional sense -- the BNZ facility is small, secured, and not representative of the company's true cost of capital). Components below sum to the BASE case cost of equity; bull/bear cases adjust the top-line risk premium up or down for de-risking/further deterioration.

component_notes.base_nz_small_cap_cost_of_equity: NZ risk-free rate + equity risk premium + generic small-cap size premium
component_notes.illiquidity_premium: Thinly traded NZX micro-cap, ~$4.9m market cap, narrow free float
component_notes.pre_profitability_burn_premium: Going-concern-relevant cash burn; company has never earned a profit from continuing operations; ~12-15 months runway at 31-Dec-2025 burn rate
component_notes.concentration_premium: Reliance on one unnamed 'largest' NZ retail partner and one China licensee for a disproportionate share of growth
component_notes.governance_execution_premium: Track record of capital destruction at this specific entity ($36m King Honey acquisition written off via 2025 receivership); near-doubling of share count in the past 12 months to keep the lights on

wacc_rationale.note: All three sit at or above the instructed 20-25% band except bull (18.5%), which is deliberately set slightly lower to reflect a scenario where proof points (sustained EBITDA profitability, warrant exercise without a discounted raise) have materially de-risked the equity relative to today.

warrants_treatment.current_moneyness: Series 1 is OUT-OF-THE-MONEY: share price $0.052 vs $0.06 strike as of valuation date.
warrants_treatment.modelling_approach: Modelled CONDITIONALLY per scenario, not as a constant assumption. In BULL, both series clear the strike ahead of their windows (Series 1 exercises in FY2027, Series 2 in FY2028) -- shares increase by the full 94.522m AND cash increases by 94.522m x $0.06 = $5.671m, both effects included together. In BASE, Series 1 expires worthless (price has not cleared $0.06 by Oct-2026 -- breakeven is not yet proven) forcing a discounted placement in FY2027 to bridge the cash shortfall (27.489m new shares at an assumed $0.045 placement price, raising $1.237m), after which improving fundamentals let Series 2 clear the strike in FY2028 (47.261m shares, $2.836m cash in). In BEAR, BOTH series expire worthless and the company instead relies on a sequence of increasingly distressed placements (assumed $0.025/share) to maintain a minimal $0.3m cash buffer through the projection window, taking the share count to 217.162m by Year 5 -- reflecting the going-concern risk flagged by the Board's own disclosure, which explicitly leans on the warrants as a funding backstop.

inputs.note_h1_2026_headline_net_income: H1-2026 reported NetIncome of +3.219m INCLUDES a one-off non-cash $4.143m gain on King Honey deconsolidation. Continuing-operations result was a LOSS of $0.902m and is what this model uses. Do not treat the headline figure as earnings.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable -- no material SBC disclosed in the CSV for recent periods (StockBasedComp is 0.0 in FY2025 and H1-2026); not a material adjustment for this company given the pre-profitability path-to-breakeven structure of the model

historical_growth.note: Per-share CAGRs (EPS, book value per share) are NOT computed. Two share consolidations (1-for-5 Apr-2020, 1-for-100 Jan-2024) plus a near-doubling of the share count via the Nov-2025 rights issue mean SharesOutstanding is not a continuous series -- FY2020's 1,824.55m and FY2024's 54.32m shares differ by ~500x from consolidations, not buybacks or dilution. Computing EPS or equity-per-share CAGRs across these breaks would be meaningless. EPS/equity CAGRs at the aggregate (non-per-share) level are also not meaningful because the company has never earned a profit from continuing operations and total equity swung from +$4.3m (FY2020) to -$2.3m (FY2025) to +$3.1m (H1-2026) on one-off items (King Honey losses, then its deconsolidation gain), not organic compounding.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: not applicable -- see path-to-breakeven scenario model in `projections` and `valuation` instead of a historical-CAGR-driven DCF
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable -- standard CAGR-based growth selection is not used for this ticker.

base.warrant_outcome: Series 1 expires worthless (FY2027); discounted placement (27.489m shares @ $0.045) bridges the shortfall; Series 2 exercises in FY2028 (47.261m shares, $2.836m cash in)
base.narrative: Revenue grows but decelerates as international scale-up proves harder than the recent guidance-raise momentum implies; EBITDA breakeven reached around FY2028-29; one further modest dilutive raise required to bridge the gap ahead of Series 2 exercising.

bull.warrant_outcome: Both series exercise (Series 1 FY2027, Series 2 FY2028) -- price clears $0.06 well ahead of each window; full $5.671m combined proceeds received, no dilutive placement needed
bull.narrative: Malaysia/SE Asia and China licensing scale faster than guided, NZ shelf-space gains continue, EBITDA breakeven pulled forward to FY2027-28, and the improving trajectory re-rates the stock above the $0.06 strike in time for both warrant series to fund growth without a discounted raise.

bear.exit_method: still EBITDA-negative at Year 5; valued at 0.3x Year-5 revenue as a distressed-brand floor rather than an EV/EBITDA multiple
bear.warrant_outcome: Both series expire worthless (price never clears $0.06); company relies on a sequence of increasingly distressed placements (assumed $0.025/share) to maintain a bare minimum cash buffer, taking shares to 217.162m by Year 5
bear.narrative: International traction disappoints, the largest retail partner or China licensee relationship deteriorates, breakeven keeps slipping, both warrant series expire worthless, and the company is forced into repeated deep-discount raises. A meaningful probability mass within this scenario is a going-concern failure / near-total loss of equity value -- reflected by flooring the per-share output at $0.00 rather than reporting a negative number, and by this scenario carrying the largest single probability weight (35%) in the blend.

valuation.terminal_value_method: Exit EV/EBITDA multiple on Year-5 EBITDA (Gordon-growth perpetuity is not used -- FCF/EBITDA are near zero through most of the projection window, making a growth-perpetuity terminal value numerically unstable). Bear case exits EBITDA-negative and is instead valued at 0.3x Year-5 revenue.

bear.exit_method: 0.3x Year-5 revenue (distressed floor, EBITDA still negative)
bear.intrinsic_value_note: Raw calculation implies negative equity value, i.e. the modelled going-concern/dilution path more than exhausts shareholder equity. Floored at $0.00/share (a limited-liability equity claim cannot be negative) rather than reported as a negative number. This reflects a genuine, non-trivial probability of near-total loss in this scenario, consistent with the Board's own going-concern disclosure.

entry_price.method: Base-case interim owner FCF (Years 1-5, including negative early years, carried through honestly) discounted at 15%, plus the base-case terminal value (still built with the 21% cost-of-equity exit multiple, as the fair price a buyer pays at exit) discounted back to today at 15%, less Year-5 net debt, divided by the Year-5 projected share count.

base.note: Entry price ($0.0200) sits ABOVE the base-case intrinsic value ($0.0144) because the 15% hurdle is below the 21% base cost of equity used for intrinsic value -- consistent with the repo's standard sanity property (lower discount rate => higher present value), even though both figures are well below the current $0.052 price given the modelled dilution.

sensitivity.note: Sensitivity run on BASE case: cost of equity vs. exit EV/EBITDA multiple (Gordon terminal growth is not used in this model, so the standard terminal-growth axis is replaced with the exit multiple).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base carries the largest single weight as the most likely path given two consecutive guidance raises and a halving of the continuing-operations loss H1-2025 to H1-2026 -- but bear is weighted higher than a default 25% given ~12-15 months of cash runway, a warrant backstop that is currently out-of-the-money, and this specific management team's history of capital destruction at this entity (the $36m King Honey write-off). Bull is weighted lowest -- it requires BOTH international scale-up to outperform guidance AND the share price to clear the $0.06 strike twice on schedule.

disclosures.reason: Company has never generated positive FCF or continuing-operations profit; per-share history broken by two share consolidations and a near-doubling share issuance; see valuation_philosophy.
key_near_term_catalysts: Audited FY2026 results (year to 30-Jun-2026), due to NZX before 31 August 2026 -- will confirm whether the twice-raised gross revenue (>$7.4m) and EBITDA loss (<$1.6m) guidance was met

Series 1 warrant window, 1-30 October 2026: 47.261m warrants at $0.06 strike are currently out-of-the-money against a $0.052 share price -- whether the stock re-rates above $0.06 before this window closes determines a major funding and dilution branch point
disclosures.going_concern_flag: Company's own filings cite going-concern dependence on continued BNZ facility support, existing cash, and the warrants as a funding backstop. ~12-15 months of runway at the 31-Dec-2025 burn rate absent a step-change in profitability or fresh capital.
